html:
Maximiliano Hernández Martínez was a Salvadoran general who ruled El Salvador as dictator from 1931 to 1944. His army carried out the massacre of 1932.

He came to power in a coup in December 1931. Weeks later he crushed the peasant rising in the west, and the killings known as La Matanza followed. He then ruled with a mix of order and eccentricity: he was a believer in the occult and once had the street lamps of the capital covered with coloured paper to fight an epidemic.

He built roads and a central bank but allowed no opposition. A general strike of students and workers forced him out in 1944, and he fled to Honduras, where he was killed by his driver in 1966. He was the first of a line of officers who ruled El Salvador until 1979, like Carías in Honduras and Somoza in Nicaragua.
sum: Maximiliano Hernández Martínez was a Salvadoran general who ruled El Salvador as dictator from 1931 to 1944. His army carried out the massacre of 1932.
